places.now: Le Môle, a peak of about 1,863 m in Haute-Savoie
places.reason: The Môle is the well-known peak near Bonneville, visible from Geneva and the Lake Léman shores, and the gazetteer's Landes mill is unrelated.

places.now: The Montalègre lakeside slope below Cologny, near the former Maison Chapuis and Villa Diodati
places.reason: Shelley lodged at Maison Chapuis on the Montalègre shore in 1816 and the novel uses the name for this stretch of lakeside; the gazetteer's quay in Cologny is the right area but only approximate.

places.now: Pentland Hills Regional Park, south-west of Edinburgh
places.reason: This is a range, so the point is a central spot near Carnethy Hill and Scald Law, the highest ground; the gazetteer's match is correct but marks only one edge near Carlops.

places.now: Pont Pélissier over the Arve gorge between Les Houches and Servoz
places.reason: The route from Sallanches to Chamonix crosses the Arve near here, but I know the area rather than the exact spot of the bridge.

places.now: Mont Blanc massif, on the French-Italian border
places.reason: The Alps of Savoy are a range seen from Geneva, so I chose Mont Blanc, their best-known peak, as the representative point.

places.now: Central Asia, parts of Kazakhstan, Mongolia, and southern Siberia
places.reason: Tartary was an imprecise European name for the steppe lands of inner and northern Asia, so this is only a rough central point; the gazetteer's French hamlet is a modern namesake.

places.place_id: ennis unclear county town where the assizes were held
places.now: no certain site; the novel does not name the Irish county town
places.reason: Shelley never names the Irish coastal town or the county town, so the setting is invented and any particular town such as Galway or Ennis would be guesswork.

places.now: Danube floodplain woodland south-east of Ingolstadt, Bavaria
places.reason: The novel gives no exact site for this forest, so this is a guess based on the Danube forests near Ingolstadt, and the gazetteer's street is a modern namesake.

places.now: Urnersee, the south-eastern arm of Lake Lucerne
places.reason: Lake Uri is the Urnersee between Brunnen and Flüelen, so the point is mid-lake, and the gazetteer's Lake Lucerne match is the parent lake near Gersau.

places.now: Orreaga/Roncesvalles, a pass and village in Navarre
places.reason: This is the Pyrenean pass of the Chanson de Roland battle, and the gazetteer's village is the correct place.

places.now: no certain site; the villa is invented, and Lake Como is only a general setting
places.reason: Villa Lavenza is Shelley's invention and named for Elizabeth's family, with no real building identified, so Bellagio on Lake Como is only a rough area guess.
